Story & Plot

Following the disappearance of the benevolent King, the Evil Queen rules a once fair land with a cruel streak. When the Queen attempts to kill Princess Snow White out of jealousy over her inner beauty, the princess flees deep into the dark woods. There, she encounters seven magical dwarves and a young bandit named Jonathan as they strive to survive the Queen's relentless pursuit and take back the kingdom.

Comedy & Entertainment

The film leans into a childlike, grade-school mood that offers moments of fun and surprising joy for some viewers. While not a comedy in the traditional sense, it aims for a lighthearted and innocent tone in its first half. Gal Gadot also brings moments of campy fun to her role as the villain. Overall, the entertainment value relies on its classic fairy tale premise and upbeat musical numbers rather than traditional comedic set pieces.

Performances & Direction

Rachel Zegler delivers an appealingly earnest portrayal as Snow White, backed by a gorgeous singing voice suited for the film's childlike mood. Gal Gadot offers some moments of campy fun as the antagonist, though some reviewers found both lead actresses a bit wooden and non-emotive. The cast also features Andrew Burnap, Andrew Barth Feldman, and Jeremy Swift in supporting roles.

Strengths

  • Gorgeous singing voice from Rachel Zegler
  • First half projects a bracing innocence and joy
  • Relatable central theme of oppression versus kindness
  • Moments of campy fun from the villain
  • Some memorable musical numbers

Weaknesses

Unfortunately, the promising moments are undercut by other story elements, and some reviewers feel the method of adapting animated classics is running out of gas. Terrible CGI makes everything look plasticky and strange, leading to awkward interactions with fake little men and animals. Additionally, the simplistic setup and grade-school vibes may not satisfy audiences looking for a deeply clever or groundbreaking narrative.

Final verdict

Snow White is a mixed bag that exceeds some low expectations while largely sticking to a familiar, simplistic formula. It may offer enough sheer joy and fun musical moments for younger audiences or dedicated fans, but the plasticky CGI and uneven storytelling hold it back. Viewers should calibrate their expectations accordingly before heading into the dark woods with the princess and her companions.
